facts.statement: Fossils were discovered in 2001 and excavated in 2003 near Porvenir de Jalpa in Coahuila, Mexico.
facts.quote: Fossils of Coahuilaceratops were discovered by Claudio de Leon near the town of Porvenir de Jalpa in the south of Coahuila, Mexico in 2001 and excavated in 2003.

facts.statement: The holotype consists mainly of unarticulated skull bones from an adult, including horncores and parts of the frill.
facts.quote: The holotype CPC 276 is represented mainly by unarticulated bones of the skull of an adult individual: rostral bone, left premaxilla, right maxilla, fused nasal bones, incomplete left and right supraorbital horncores, part of the parietosquasomal frill, predentary, both dentaries, and unprepared postcranial material.

facts.statement: The species was formally described in 2010 by a team of paleontologists including Mark A. Loewen and Scott D. Sampson.
facts.quote: Coahuilaceratops magnacuerna was formally described by paleontologists Mark A. Loewen, Scott D. Sampson, Eric K. Lund, Andrew A. Farke, Martha Aguillón Martínez, Claudio A. de Leon, Rubén A. Rodríguez de la Rosa, Michael A. Getty, and David A. Eberth in 2010.

facts.statement: The genus contains only one known species, Coahuilaceratops magnacuerna.
facts.quote: It contains a single species, Coahuilaceratops magnacuerna.

facts.statement: It is the first dinosaur species described from the Cerro Huerta Formation.
facts.quote: This makes Coahuilaceratops the first dinosaur described from the Cerro Huerta Formation.

facts.statement: Adults were estimated to be about 22 feet long, 6 to 7 feet tall, with a 6-foot skull and 3 to 4-foot horns, weighing four to five tons.
facts.quote: an adult Coahuilaceratops was about 22 ft long, 6 to 7 ft tall at the shoulders and hips, with a 6 ft skull and 3 to 4 ft horns, and probably weighed about four to five tons.

facts.statement: The robust shape of its horns, lacking constriction at the tip, resembles large Pentaceratops more than Agujaceratops.
facts.quote: The hyperrobust morphology of the horns of Coahuilaceratops (relative lack of constriction in the distal region) is more reminiscent of large specimens of Pentaceratops than of Agujaceratops.

facts.statement: Despite incomplete remains, it is believed to have possessed some of the largest horns of any known dinosaur, rivaling those of Triceratops and Torosaurus.
facts.quote: Aunque se basa en restos incompletos, se cree que Coahuilaceratops posee uno de los cuernos más grandes de cualquier dinosaurio actualmente conocido, que rivaliza en tamaño absoluto con los de chasmosaurinídos más grandes como Triceratops y Torosaurus.

facts.statement: Its horns are estimated to have been up to 1.2 meters long.
facts.quote: Se estima que sus cuernos han sido de hasta 1,2 metros largo.

facts.statement: The specimen stood about two meters tall and was four meters long.
facts.quote: El ejemplar medía unos dos metros de altura y cuatro metros de longitud.

facts.statement: Loewen et al. (2010) placed it in a polytomy with Anchiceratops and Arrhinoceratops, forming a sister clade to Triceratopsini.
facts.quote: In the phylogenetic analysis performed by the authors of the Coauilaceratops description, Loewen et al. (2010), it was found in a polytomy with Anchiceratops and Arrhinoceratops, with which it was found in a sister clade of Triceratopsini.

facts.statement: Brown & Henderson (2015) analyzed it as a sister genus to Bravoceratops within a clade of non-triceratopsin chasmosaurines.
facts.quote: According to analysis conducted by Brown & Henderson (2015), Coahuiceratops is a sister genus of Bravoceratops within a clade that includes a number of other non-triceratopsin chasmosaurines, with Anchiceratops and Arrhinoceratops still forming a sister clade of Triceratopsini.

facts.statement: Dalman et al. (2022) found it in a polytomy with Bravoceratops and Sierraceratops, suggesting this group was endemic to southern Laramidia.
facts.quote: Dalman et al. (2022) found Coahuilaceratops in a polytomy with Bravoceratops and Sierraceratops. The researchers suggested that a clade containing these three genera was endemic to southern Laramidia.

facts.statement: It is a member of the subfamily Chasmosaurinae.
facts.quote: Coahuilaceratops es un miembro de la subfamilia Chasmosaurinae.

facts.statement: It forms a clade with Bravoceratops and Sierraceratops, which Dalman et al. suggested was endemic to southern Laramidia.
facts.quote: En 2021 fue descrito Sierraceratops y se encontró que forma un clado con Coahuilaceratops y Bravoceratops, y sus descriptores, Sebastian Dalman et al., sugirieron que formaban un clado endémico del sur de Laramidia.

facts.statement: Paleontologist Claudio De León found remains of two individuals, an adult and a juvenile.
facts.quote: El paleontólogo Claudio De León halló los restos de dos individuos, un adulto y un juvenil.

facts.statement: Remains were found in the Mexican state of Coahuila.
facts.quote: Sus restos se encontraron en el estado mexicano de Coahuila.

facts.statement: The collected material, mainly skull fragments, allowed the erection of the genus, noted for its characteristic large horns.
facts.quote: El material colectado corresponde principalmente a fragmentos del cráneo, lo que permitió erigir el género Coahuilaceratops magnacuerna, que tiene unos característicos cuernos grandes en la cabeza.

facts.statement: It was formally described in 2010, though it appeared as an informal nomen nudum in 2008.
facts.quote: Se describió formalmente en 2010, aunque apareció como una designación informal, nomen nudum, ya en 2008.

facts.statement: The genus name derives from the toponym Coahuila.
facts.quote: El nombre del género proviene del topónimo Coahuila

facts.statement: It is considered the sister taxon to Bravoceratops, which was found in Texas, USA.
facts.quote: Coahuilaceratops sería el taxón hermano de Bravoceratops, hallado en Texas, Estados Unidos.

facts.statement: It lived in the Late Cretaceous, between 71 and 70 million years ago in the Maastrichtian, in what is now North America.
facts.quote: que vivió en el Cretácico Superior, entre 71 a 70 millones de años en el Maastrichtiano, en lo que hoy es Norteamérica.

facts.statement: All specimens were collected from a single location in the middle layer of the Cerro Huerta Formation, dating to 71.5 to 70.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Todos los ejemplares de Coahuilaceratops fueron recolectados de un solo lugar en el estrato medio de la Formación Cerro Huerta, que data de hace entre 71.5 y 70.5 millones de años.

facts.statement: The fossil record spans the Maastrichtian stage from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

rejected.quote: about 71.5 to 70.5 million years ago in what is now northern Mexico.
